finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> route has no authentication or ownership check, so any caller who can reach it can read any invoice by ID, including the customer field.
finding.source: inv_id path parameter (invoices.py:8), supplied by any client that can reach the route.
finding.sink: INVOICES.get(inv_id) and jsonify(inv) returning the full invoice record (invoices.py:9-10).

trace.note: Route /invoice/<inv_id> registered with no auth decorator.
Handler takes inv_id from the URL.
Dict lookup in INVOICES with no check on the caller's identity or ownership.
Entire invoice record returned as JSON, including the customer field.

finding.guards_checked: No login, role, or ownership check on this route. No before_request hook or decorator in this file. The sibling routes /my/invoice (invoices.py:16) and /my/invoices (invoices.py:23) do ownership checks, but this route does not. Exploitability depends on how invoice IDs are generated (sequential or guessable IDs make enumeration easy); random IDs reduce but do not remove the risk. Global auth middleware, if any, is not in this directory and would still not restrict results to the caller's own invoices.

verdict.guard_found: none. invoices.py:7 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no auth decorator. invoices.py:9 is a bare dict lookup with abort(404) only for a missing ID, not an ownership check. invoices.py:10 returns the full record via jsonify. Grep for before_request, login_required, g.user assignment, and after_request found nothing, and invoices.py is the only file in the directory. The ownership check at invoices.py:16-17 exists only in the sibling route /my/invoice/<inv_id>.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: invoices.py:7-10 returns any invoice by ID with no identity or ownership check, so an anonymous caller can read any record including the customer field (invoices.py:16 shows records carry a customer key), while the sibling routes at invoices.py:14-17 and 22-23 do enforce ownership. The one caveat is that global middleware outside this directory could not be inspected, but nothing in this directory would stop the request.
